item.title: Beppu Hells (Jigoku Meguri) — Guide
item.description: The ‘Hells of Beppu’ (Beppu Jigoku) are a collection of spectacular hot springs — not for bathing, but for viewing — that are the signature attraction of Japan’s greatest onsen town. Over centuries these fiercely hot, mineral-rich springs, bubbling up from the volcanic earth with clouds of steam, were so violent and forbidding that locals called them ‘jigoku’ (hells). Today seven of them are developed for sightseeing, each with a dramatically different character: the stunning cobalt-blue Umi Jigoku (‘sea hell’), the seething blood-red Chinoike Jigoku (‘blood pond hell’), a geyser that erupts regularly, mud pools, and the popular Kamado Jigoku (‘furnace hell’), which showcases several types of colourful springs, steam vents and foot baths together, with stalls selling hell-steamed snacks and eggs.
